label: early-position k/p/w/d/m/a/r/s input (orig steps 1-3, or orig(0) re-fed at first copy step)
explanation: Reset-gate unit driven by the current input token being one of a graded set (k > p > w > d > m ~ a ~ r > s > l ~ b; nearly zero for q, t and the rest), gated by how early in the sequence it is. Its activity is highest at original steps 1-2 (k/p at step 1 fire 100% of the time, ~90% at step 2). It is weaker at step 3 and at the first copy step after the delimiter (recall_idx 1, where the input is orig(0)), and almost silent from original step 4 on, at step 0, at the delimiter step, and in later copy steps. Magnitude follows the token ranking and falls with position. Prior context also matters: at step 3 / first copy step it fires much more reliably when earlier tokens include j/e/h/1/f (e.g. k/p at step 3 after first token j fire 97% of the time), and less often when an earlier input was already in the driving set. The binary predicate cannot capture this graded additive token x position x context structure, so precision is about 0.65; the looser version (any of k,p,w,d,m,a,r,s,l,b at steps 1-3 or recall 1) covers 95% of mass but has 0.45 precision.
